findings.issue: Round-1 finding 1 is only half fixed. Making `holdsCancelClaim()` false for FAILED covers siblings that freeze while S1 is already FAILED. It does not cover a sibling that froze while S1 was still REQUESTED, before S1's card leg came back FAILED. That sibling saw S1 as covered, became completing, and froze the remainder plus `shippingAmount`. `Order.advanceShipment` then drops S1's FAILED claim and ships it, so the sibling keeps (or later pays) shipping on an order that is never fully cancelled. Two reachable paths. (a) The case I named in round 1, still open: a whole cancel claims S1, S2 and S3 in one T1 (S3 completing with shipping). S2's card leg reports FAILED and the loop stops with S3 still REQUESTED. S2 is shipped (claim dropped). A retry of S3 reuses its frozen claim and refunds shipping while S2 is delivered. (b) A seller's S1 cancel hits a timeout and stays REQUESTED. S2 is cancelled: completing, shipping refunded, DONE. The S1 retry is reported FAILED, and S1 is shipped. The remainder items stay correct to rounding (S1's old share equals its pro-rata), so the leak is the shipping fee. This is still an AC-7 money error. The new test `failedClaim_siblingCancelNotCompleting_shipWins` covers only the FAILED-first ordering.
findings.fix: In `Order.advanceShipment`, before `s.dropFailedCancel()`, refuse with 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT ("cancel must be completed") when `s` has a FAILED claim and any other shipment holds a claim (REQUESTED or DONE) with `cancelShippingRefund > 0`. The operator then retries the cancel, and the re-freeze gives S1 its remainder with no shipping, as it does now. Add two ITs: whole cancel with S2 FAILED and S3 REQUESTED-completing, then ship S2 gives 409; and S1 REQUESTED, then S2 completing DONE, then S1 FAILED, then ship S1 gives 409.

findings.issue: The note is now silently cut to 500 chars in the entity. This was not one of the review findings, but it is reasonable: a 500-char reason plus the prefix overflowed varchar(500) and failed T3 after money had moved. A `@Size` on `CancelOrder.reason` would reject the overflow at the edge instead.
findings.fix: Optional: add `@Size(max = 450)` to `AdminRequests.CancelOrder.reason` and keep the truncation as a backstop.

summary: Most round-1 findings are fixed at 8f214e7. The dropped FAILED claim now bumps the attempt, so the next claim uses the next key (tested). The uncovered COD wallet part is recorded through `addRefunded` and COD_PENDING is kept (tested). The seller id is resolved once in the controller. AC-3 tests now assert no CANCELLED history row. `creditBack` reuses `enqueue`, and the repository uses imports. Line count (576) and verification (pending, Docker down) are set aside per the CEO. On the question asked: the FAILED-claim change introduces no double count. A FAILED claim is excluded from coverage, the remainder sum and the leg siblings, and a reclaim re-freezes it under the next attempt key. When it re-freezes, any sibling that froze in between is counted as covered. So the re-frozen share is either pro-rata or exactly paidItems minus the other item parts. Shipping is taken only if no other claim or return carries it, and the wallet and card legs stay capped by W and the card room. A key never carries two different amounts. The fix does not cover the reverse ordering, though: a sibling that froze as completing while S1 was REQUESTED keeps the shipping after S1 goes FAILED and is shipped. This includes the whole-cancel case named in round 1 (S2 FAILED, S3 REQUESTED-completing). That remains a major money error under AC-7, so I am requesting changes. A small 409 guard in `Order.advanceShipment` with two ITs would close it.
